display.title: Keep On Dancing: The Mitteler Rebbe and the Power of Simcha (Adar)
display.summary_short: What if you are not in the mood to be happy in Adar? The storyteller explains how to bring on simcha, and tells how the Mitteler Rebbe used joy to cancel a decree against his son.
display.summary_long: In a leap year with two months of Adar, sixty days of extra simcha, the storyteller asks: what if I am just not in the mood? He shares the Tzemach Tzedek's advice in his letters: always be happy, and even pretend to be happy, because the heart follows one's actions. The Frierdiker Rebbe taught that once you decide to be happy, Hashem sends new reasons for joy; thanking Hashem makes us happy, and simcha sweetens harsh judgments. Then the story: the Mitteler Rebbe had a choir and musicians, and Chassidim who put on a horse-riding show like Cossacks, all saved for special days. One ordinary weekday he suddenly called for a great celebration. In the middle, his son Reb Nochum fell from his galloping horse, but the Mitteler Rebbe signaled for even more music. The injury turned out to be minor. The Mitteler Rebbe later explained that he had seen a decree against his son's life, and that joy is the strongest way to remove it, so he increased the simcha to remove every trace.
display.lesson: Simcha breaks through every bad decree; in Adar, choose to be happy, thank Hashem, and do things that bring joy to you and your family.

date.note: "Two months of Adar... 60 days of simcha": told around Adar I of a leap year; no year given.
